guidance.procedure: Resolve the relation by matching the actor, operative action, protected object, modality, trigger, exception and quantifier. Entailment requires language establishing the proposition; Contradiction requires an incompatible operative rule. Related language, silence, or a missing permission is not automatically contradiction. Then collect every complete responsive provision, including any lead-in, definition, exception introduction, continuation or referenced trigger needed to preserve force and scope. Include repeated provisions that independently resolve the issue; exclude headings and merely contextual clauses. Search the whole contract before selecting NotMentioned, and return no evidence for that label because a local excerpt cannot prove absence.

operations.rationale: Historical answers frequently found the right relation but omitted governing or repeated members, while other answers over-selected adjacent clauses. A witness is intentionally omitted because no excerpt can demonstrate whole-contract absence and the narrower records carry the useful positive and opposing examples.

guidance.procedure: Read the entire operative definition. Technical-only coverage requires an exhaustive subject-matter definition confined to technical categories; business, financial, commercial, personnel, customer, contractual or marketing matter contradicts it. Transmission form does not determine subject matter. For explicit identification, ask whether every protected disclosure must be marked, designated, identified or confirmed. Coverage based alternatively on reasonable understanding, confidential circumstances, or protection whether or not marked contradicts universal identification. For verbal coverage, require an operative oral, spoken or verbal mode, or an unmistakably comprehensive tangible-and-intangible formulation; include any identification or later-confirmation conditions.

operations.rationale: The paired evidence preserves the decisive identification contrast: universal mode-specific identification versus coverage whether or not labeled. Historical errors also show that broad subject matter and transmission mode must not be conflated.

guidance.procedure: Analyze the disposition trigger separately from what may remain afterward. A duty tied to termination, expiration, project completion, abandoned discussions or another stated ending event supports termination-related return or destruction; a request-only duty does not inherit a trigger from a separate duration clause. Return alone is sufficient. For post-disposition possession, an express archival, legal, backup, regulatory, dispute or record-retention exception supports possession. An exhaustive command covering all protected information and copies, without a retention exception, contradicts it; a command limited to documents or another subset is unresolved. Include the complete trigger, all disposition alternatives and every applicable carve-out.

operations.rationale: The witnesses contrast an express legally required retention exception with an exhaustive return-or-destroy command. Historical answers repeatedly imported termination into request-only duties or inferred retention from silence.

guidance.procedure: Require an operative disclosure or access permission and identify its recipient class. Employees support employee sharing. Consultants, advisers, contractors, agents, affiliates and comparable outside representatives support third-party sharing only when the clause actually authorizes them to receive the information; a definition or description of status is not permission. Preserve need-to-know, purpose, consent and confidentiality conditions. An express ban reaching the class, with disclosure available only after separate approval or accession, opposes present permission. A generic disclosure ban that does not address the class is unresolved. Exclude neighboring security, password and market-restriction provisions.

operations.rationale: The evidence supplies a direct contrast between need-to-know disclosure to employees and consultants and a clause withholding disclosure unless recipients separately accept terms and obtain approval. Historical answers often confused status or generic security language with authority to share.

guidance.procedure: Locate the particular exception or permission and its governing introduction. Independent development requires development without use of, reference to, benefit from or access to protected information; public-domain, compelled-disclosure and third-party-source clauses do not substitute for it. Third-party acquisition requires information received, furnished, obtained or acquired from a lawful outside source not bound by confidentiality or transmission restrictions; outgoing disclosure permission concerns a different action. Include all stated conditions. A direct prohibition opposes the proposition; absence of the particular limb remains unresolved.

operations.rationale: The selected evidence separately demonstrates the development act and the incoming-source act, preventing the recurrent historical substitution of one exception for the other.

guidance.procedure: Keep entitlement separate from permitted use. No-rights entailment requires an express denial of license, title, ownership, intellectual-property rights, right of use or another interest; sole ownership is sufficient only when the clause also excludes recipient rights. A purpose-limited permission does not contradict a denial of proprietary rights. Limited-use entailment requires an operative sole-purpose limitation or prohibition on other use, including a construction clause preserving only a purpose-bound use right. Ownership, return, nondisclosure and security duties alone do not establish limited use. Scan for and include every independent operative use restriction.

operations.rationale: One witness supplies a complete no-right-or-license construction and the other a concise operative business-purpose limitation. Historical answers sometimes treated ownership as a use restriction or limited use as a proprietary grant.

guidance.procedure: For reverse engineering, require an operative ban on reverse engineering, decompiling, disassembling, reconstruction or equivalent analysis of materials embodying protected information; a copying ban alone is insufficient. For copying, distinguish permission from prohibition: an express right, a necessary-copy exception, a consent-based exception or permission to retain a copy supports copying in some circumstances. An unqualified no-copy or no-retention rule opposes it. Legend preservation and storage controls merely regulate existing copies unless they also authorize or prohibit creation. Include the actor-bearing lead-in and any exception governing the verb series.

operations.rationale: The witnesses provide a direct reverse-engineering prohibition and an opposed no-copy rule. This addresses historical mistakes that treated copying and reverse engineering as interchangeable or read a prohibition as permission.

guidance.procedure: Require both legal compulsion and an operative warning duty. The trigger may be law, regulation, subpoena, court order or legal process, and the notice may occur in a later sentence. Permission to comply with law, a compelled-disclosure exclusion, or disclosure to a regulator without a notice duty is unresolved rather than contradiction. Preserve timing and legality qualifications, and include the complete trigger-plus-notice sequence; protective-order cooperation belongs only when it continues that sequence.

operations.rationale: The witness is a compact compelled-disclosure permission containing prior written information, while historical answers show that governmental disclosure alone was wrongly treated as satisfying notice.

guidance.procedure: Treat the protected object separately for each proposition. Agreement secrecy requires operative protection of the agreement, its existence or terms, negotiations, their status, discussions or the contemplated transaction; confidentiality of exchanged information and an entire-agreement clause are irrelevant. Non-solicitation requires a ban on soliciting, recruiting, hiring, inducing departure or targeted contact with specified employees, consultants or other representatives; customer or market restraints alone do not suffice. Survival requires substantive duties to continue after termination or an express post-termination period; a fixed agreement term or liability only for earlier breaches does not preserve the duties. Include class, duration, exceptions and referenced substantive provisions needed for scope.

operations.rationale: The selected evidence independently demonstrates agreement-existence protection, representative non-solicitation and continuing confidentiality duties. Keeping them in one object-focused procedure addresses historical confusion among transaction secrecy, customer restraints, agreement duration and substantive survival.

complete_original_evidence_texts: “Confidential Information” includes all business, financial, contractual, marketing and/or technical information, in whatever form embodied, which has been or may be disclosed, or to which access is provided, by a party (“Discloser”) to the other party to this Agreement (“Recipient”), which
(a) if in writing, is marked “confidential”, “proprietary” or other similar marking at the time of disclosure, or
(b) if provided orally or visually, is identified as confidential at the time of disclosure and confirmed in writing to Recipient within 15 days of such disclosure.

“Confidential Information” includes, without limitation, design documents, trade secrets, files, marketing and business plans, documentation, reports, projections, interpretations, forecasts, records (including information regarding the disclosing party’s businesses, customers, strategies, operations, finances, technology, data, processes, methodologies, know-how, existing or future products, services, applications and methods of operation (including how such methods are developed, conducted or operated)) and all other information, whether in written, oral, encoded, electronic or other tangible or intangible form, and whether or not labeled, marked or otherwise identified as “Confidential” upon disclosure thereof, relating to the disclosing party’s products and businesses, and any other information that would, if disclosed to any actual or potential competitors of the disclosing party, give or increase those competitors’ advantage over the disclosing party or directly or indirectly harm the disclosing party’s business.
